claim: Sluis is a fortress shopping town with over 150 shops and 45 restaurants/cafés, attracting around 5 million annual visitors, with shops open on Sundays and holidays (closed only Christmas Day and New Year's Day).
quote: Sluis is a comfortable and atmospheric shopping town with over 150 shops and 45 restaurants/cafés... shops open on Sundays and holidays (except Christmas and New Year's Day)... approximately 5 million annual visitors

claim: Sluis received city rights in 1290, was captured by Spanish troops in 1587 during the Eighty Years' War, retaken in 1604, and was home to the Michelin three-star Oud Sluis from 2006 to 2013.
quote: During the Eighty Years' War in 1587 the town was captured by Spanish troops under the Duke of Parma... Oud Sluis, a Michelin three-star restaurant from 2006-2013

claim: Since the early 20th century Sluis has been a Sunday-shopping magnet for Belgians because Dutch shops open on Sundays while Belgian shops typically don't, and drugstore items are cheaper across the border.
quote: Since the beginning of the 20th century, Sluis has gained in popularity among Belgian day-trippers to come shopping on Sundays as - in contrast to Belgium - the shops are open then in Sluis

claim: Sluis's De Brak windmill, built in 1739 on a 2.5 m mill-belt, is a round stone scaffolding mill converted to grist-milling and the first stone mill of Sluis.
quote: De Brak, named after a dog breed, was built in 1739 and is located on a 2.5 m high millbelt. The Brak is a round stone scaffolding mill that has been converted into a grist mill

claim: Sluis has the only town hall in the Netherlands with a Flemish belfry, dating to the 14th century, with 142 steps to a panoramic viewing platform, now also housing an interactive museum.
quote: the only town hall in the Netherlands with a belfort - a Flemish clock-tower - situated at the very heart of the town, dating back to the 14th century and now housing an interactive museum

claim: Restaurant Demain in the Strandhotel Cadzand-Bad, opened January 2024 by chef Dani Hoefnagels (formerly Pure C sous-chef), earned a Michelin star in its first year but will leave the Strandhotel on 31 May 2026 and continue under the same name at a new location.
quote: Restaurant Demain welcomed its first guests on January 19, 2024... awarded a Michelin star in its very first year... As of 31 May 2026, the restaurant will be saying goodbye to the Strandhotel Cadzand

claim: Pure C, Sergio Herman's two-Michelin-star Cadzand-Bad restaurant opened in 2010, closed on 23 September 2023, ending the original Cadzand-Bad fine-dining era under his Strandhotel concept.
quote: Pure C closed its doors on September 23, 2023, and the restaurant was taken over by Dani Hoefnagels

claim: Cadzand-Bad is the southernmost seaside resort of the Netherlands, with five 4-star hotels, an officially-accredited seaside health spa designation, and a marina (opened spring 2017) offering 125 mooring places.
quote: Five 4-star hotels... A marina that opened in spring 2017 offers 125 mooring places as the southernmost marina of the Netherlands... given official accreditation as a 'seaside health spa resort'

claim: Aardenburg's archaeological museum has relocated to a larger building at Sint Bavostraat 3 under the new name Cultuurforum Aardenburg, displaying finds from the town's importance as a Roman fortress (150-275 AD) with foundations of a small Roman temple in the garden.
quote: The archaeological museum has relocated to a larger building at Sint Bavostraat 3 and is now named Cultuurforum Aardenburg

claim: Aardenburg was a particularly important Roman fortress between roughly 150 and 275 AD, making it one of the few sites in Zeeland with substantive Roman archaeology accessible to visitors.
quote: Aardenburg was between 150 and 275 A.D. a particularly important Roman fortress

claim: Retranchement is a 295-resident village right on the Belgian border, named after the 1622 fortifications built by Prince Maurice of Orange to secure the recently-captured port of Sluis; Fort Nassau and the 1630 garrison church survive.
quote: It was 'first mentioned in 1627 as Een groot en seer sterck Retrenchement'... Prince Maurice of Orange constructed the original fortification around 1622 to defend against Spanish forces

claim: Retranchement is the south-westernmost coastal village in the Netherlands, with intact 17th-century star-fort ramparts and bastions you can walk along the top of, bordering the Zwin nature reserve.
quote: Retranchement lies in the far west of Zeeuws-Vlaanderen... the south-westernmost coastal village in the Netherlands. The village borders Belgium and sits on the edge of the nature reserve Het Zwin

claim: The Westerschelde Ferry runs Breskens-Vlissingen 365 days a year as a pedestrian/cyclist-only ferry, with a 23-minute crossing and roughly half-hourly departures during the high-season timetable in force until 6 September 2026.
quote: Until 6 September 2026, crossings will run according to the high season timetable... Departures roughly every 30 minutes, starting at 6:18 AM through 10:18 PM

claim: The Netherlands has reintroduced temporary, non-systematic border controls with Belgium since 9 December 2024, extended to mid-2026, so drivers crossing Knokke-Sluis may occasionally encounter Marechaussee checks rather than the long-standing open-border norm.
quote: The Netherlands has implemented temporary border controls at its internal borders with other Schengen countries, which commenced on 9 December 2024

claim: Knokke-Heist to Breskens is approximately 27-28 km by road, around a 29-minute drive, putting Breskens just inside the 30 km radius from Knokke.
quote: The driving distance between Knokke-Heist and Breskens is approximately 17 miles, and it takes approximately 29 minutes to drive

claim: Cadzand-Bad lies under 10 km from Knokke-Heist (straight-line 8.96 km), making it the closest Dutch resort and an easy 15-minute hop across the border.
quote: Cadzand and Knokke are very close to each other, with the straight-line distance being 8.96 km
